segmentation.text: Every driver of a vehicle
approaching a stop intersection indicated by a stop sign

shall stop before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is no crosswalk, shall stop at a clearly marked stop line, or if none, then at the point nearest the intersecting highway
where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway
before entering the intersection.

elements.justification: “vehicle” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines and the run admits as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, so the span claims ru.aggregate with that id: the atom is “membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id”, true where the road user carries an included class, unknown where an included or unresolved class it might carry is unobserved. Its exclusion “not a stand-in for a named road-user class” does not apply, because the admitted aggregate is claimed as the aggregate and never replaced by a class atom; its exclusion of “a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle” is respected by reading “driver” through the vehicle's controlled motion (narrowing on this span) rather than as a member of the aggregate.

The approach is read as the ontology's section on an act due at a place before an event states it: “a road user's approach to an intersection is a carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection”. st.intersection is “the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges”, the region the words call the intersection; st.travel_region is the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over, “the union of the kinds a device can govern … a lane and the kinds that refine it, a bicycle lane or path, a roadway and the kinds that refine it, a shoulder, or an intersection”, which is exactly the set of carriers st.lane_enters admits, so each region argument of the claimed relations has a claimed kind; st.lane_enters is “the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end”, and its clause “it is entry topology: it is decided where the source records it … never inferred from distance, overlap or a road user's velocity” is why approaching is not read from heading or closing speed. dev.stop_sign is the “regulatory sign requiring a full halt”, the sign the words name, and dev.governs, “the travel regions whose traffic the device controls … or an intersection”, ties it to the carrier the vehicle approaches through, as the ontology directs (“the mark that governs that approach is one the source records as marking that carrier”); dev.governs's exclusion “not a stand-in for a position” does not apply, because the place of the halt is read from the crosswalk, the stop line or the view point in s3 and never from where the sign stands. rel.occupies is “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”, the anchor that makes the carrier the subject's own.

“shall stop” is the act: drv.motion.standstill carries the posted definition DEF-NRS-484A-255, “complete cessation from movement”, as a motion state at an observation, with the speed tolerance the sampling leaves to the observer. The first place is the crosswalk “on the near side of the intersection”: st.crosswalk is the “marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection”, and which crossing is the near one is st.entrance_of, “the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks — exactly that carrier's entrance, the line or crossing a vehicle approaching through that carrier halts at or before”, read on the same carrier st.lane_enters relates to the intersection; st.entrance_of's exclusion “not a stand-in for distance to the line” is why nearness never selects the crossing. The second place is st.stop_line, “the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device”, taken where the crosswalk's observed list of entrances excludes the carrier, as st.entrance_of's completeness clause permits. The third is the point nearest the intersecting highway, read on the carrier (st.travel_region) against the way the junction lies on: st.highway is “the entire width between the boundary lines of every way”, st.on_way “the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on — … an intersection lies on every way that meets there”, so the intersecting highway is a way the intersection lies on other than the one the carrier lies on. That the halt is at the place and on the near side of it is st.region_geometry, “the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it”, within p.stop_point_tolerance, with the side taken from prim.region_offset_along, “the signed distance … measured along a carrier's designated direction (st.lane_direction)”, whose sign gives the side as the ontology requires (“the side of the mark is read along that carrier's designated direction … never along the road user's heading”); the primitive's own inputs are not claimed again beyond st.lane_direction and st.region_geometry, which the rule also reads on their own for the direction and for the distance, since prim.region_offset_along “is a geometric quantity only … a distance to the region is read from st.region_geometry, never from this value”. rel.occupies excludes a halt whose footprint already overlaps the crossing or the junction, which the words place the halt before, and st.intersection is the region that entry concerns.

“before entering the intersection” is the event the duty is owed before: the observation at which the vehicle's footprint first overlaps the intersection region. rel.occupies is “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (… intersection …)” and st.intersection the region itself; st.intersection's exclusion “not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line — a stop before the crossing is earlier than a stop before the intersection” is precisely the distinction kept here, the crossing being the place of the act in s3 and the junction the event in this span.

operationalizations.standard: where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway
operationalizations.convention: Intersection sight-distance convention (AASHTO Green Book intersection sight distance, the departure-sight-triangle cases): a driver halted at the stopping point must be able to see along the major way at least the distance an approaching vehicle travels in the time needed to judge a gap and clear the junction. The point is adequate where st.sight_along_way, “the distance along a way, in each direction from the point of that way nearest a road user, within which another vehicle on that way could be seen from the road user's eye at the observation … the smaller of the two directions”, taken for the intersecting highway the junction lies on (st.highway with st.on_way and st.intersection), is at least p.intersecting_way_view_distance, and where a road user is on that way approaching the junction, that road user is visible from the vehicle (rel.visible, “b is visible from a: an unobstructed line of sight”). “approaching traffic” is read as the road users travelling on that way, with no class narrowing which of them must be seen, the posted definition of traffic covering “pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel”; the sight atom carries the view itself, since rel.visible “is not a stand-in for … the sight distance of a place” and st.sight_along_way is “not a stand-in for … whether an actual road user is seen”: the two together read the span's words where a road user is present and where none is. p.intersecting_way_view_distance is the only magnitude, and it is the reading's, not the words'.

applicability: The bound road user is a vehicle of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle that occupies a travel region whose entrance end is an intersection (st.lane_enters on that carrier) and that a stop sign governs (dev.stop_sign with dev.governs on that same carrier), and that enters that intersection: the stop intersection indicated by a stop sign which it approaches. Where the sign's governance of the carrier is unobserved, whether the rule applies is unknown; where the source's complete record shows the sign governs no carrier the vehicle occupies, the rule does not apply.
obligation: At each observation at which the vehicle's footprint first overlaps the intersection it approaches (the entry event: the rise of rel.occupies of the vehicle on the intersection X that the carrier it occupies runs into, st.lane_enters, read from this observation and the one before it), the vehicle must have been at a standstill (drv.motion.standstill with p.standstill_speed_tolerance) at some observation of the approach that leads to that entry, with its body at the place the words name. The place is read from the words in their order: first the crosswalk that marks the entrance of the carrier the vehicle approaches through (st.entrance_of on the same carrier st.lane_enters relates to X); where that crosswalk's entrances are observed, so that its list is complete, and exclude the carrier, the clearly marked stop line that marks it; where neither marks it, the point on the carrier nearest the intersecting highway at which the view of s4 is met. Where a mark's association with the carrier is not observed, whether that mark governs is unknown and the duty is unknown on that ground. A halt counts at the place where the distance from the vehicle's body to the mark (st.region_geometry) is within p.stop_point_tolerance and the mark lies ahead along the carrier's designated direction (the sign of prim.region_offset_along with st.lane_direction); the words placing the halt before the vehicle enters the crossing and the junction, a halt at which its footprint already overlaps that region (rel.occupies) is not at the place, and the tolerance applies outside that region only. The search for the halt runs back from the entry event and ends only at the start of that approach — the last observation before the event at which the vehicle, on a carrier the mark marks, is off the mark, short of it and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance — or at the previous entry of the same vehicle into the same intersection; nothing else ends it: not another junction or mark, not the start of the recording, not a first observation, not a distance travelled. Only an observed exit from the stopping zone upstream begins a new approach, so a vehicle that leaves the zone upstream and returns owes the halt again, while crossing the mark, moving on toward the junction, a change of carrier, a lateral move or a reverse within the zone begin none and lose no halt already made. Where the search finds the halt the duty is met; where it reaches either end without the halt the duty is violated; where it reaches neither end without finding it — the recording begins inside the stopping zone, the observation before the event does not show the vehicle's place relative to the mark through its carrier, or the speed that decides the standstill is unobserved — the duty is unknown. Each entry owes its own halt: a halt made before the previous entry of the same vehicle into the same intersection discharged that entry, not this one.

narrowings.why: “Every driver of a vehicle” is read as the vehicle whose motion is controlled. Who or what controls a road user is not observable, and the ontology reads “drives”, “operates” and “the driver” through the vehicle's controlled motion, a vehicle moving on the road being taken to be driven, with the duty binding that vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever is at the controls.

“indicated by a stop sign” is read as the presence of a stop sign governing the approach. That a sign is official or posted by an authority is a legal status the ontology reads through the feature itself: the sign's presence on the road is the evidence of the designation the section's title speaks of.

“a clearly marked stop line” is read as the stop line the scene represents. The ontology states this reading for exactly these words: the line's presence is the evidence, and the paint's clarity or wear is not modelled. The reading relaxes nothing about which place governs, the act or its timing.

“the point nearest the intersecting highway where the driver has a view” is read as a point on the carrier the vehicle approaches through, rather than any point of the scene: the words single out the vehicle's own approach, and the place is read on the region the node binds. Among the points of that carrier at which the view of s4 is met, the duty is read as met by a halt at or before the nearest such point to the intersecting highway, within p.stop_point_tolerance of it, so a halt farther back on the same carrier that still meets the view is not a violation; this is the reading of “the point nearest … where the driver has a view”, which names a nearest point among those with a view and not a single surveyed spot.

“the driver has a view of approaching traffic” is read as what could be seen along the intersecting way from where the vehicle stands, and as the visibility of a road user of the traffic aggregate that is there. What a driver perceived is not observable; the ontology directs that where the words offer observable evidence the rule reads it, “what was in an actual road user's line of sight is rel.visible; what could be seen from or at a place is st.sight_distance”, and st.sight_along_way is that quantity measured along the way for a road user at the observation.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car runs along a marked lane that the source records as entering a four-way junction, and a stop sign governs that lane. A marked crosswalk is recorded as marking that lane's entrance. From the last observation at which the car is off the crossing, short of it and more than the stop-point tolerance from it, through to the observation at which its footprint first overlaps the junction, its speed never falls to the standstill tolerance: it rolls over the crossing at about 4 m/s and enters the junction.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same approach and the same crossing. Two seconds before the crossing the car's speed falls to zero and stays there for several observations, its body short of the crossing along the lane's designated direction and within the stop-point tolerance of it, its footprint overlapping neither the crossing nor the junction; it then moves off and enters the junction.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A pedal cycle propelled by human power — a device the vehicle definition leaves out, so the aggregate is false for it — rides along the same stop-sign-governed lane and into the junction without halting anywhere. No vehicle is bound and the rule does not engage.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The forbid approach, with the source declaring the speed of road users absent: the trigger is decided (the lane, its entrance into the junction, the stop sign's governance and the entry are all recorded), but no observation of the approach decides whether the car came to a complete cessation from movement, so the search for the act neither finds it nor excludes it.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: The recording begins with the car already over the stop line and short of the junction, its body nearer the mark than the stop-point tolerance, so no observation at which it was outside the mark's stopping zone upstream is recorded; it enters the junction two observations later without halting in the recorded part. The search back from the entry reaches neither the start of the approach nor a previous entry of this car into this junction, and no recorded halt decides the duty.
scenarios.boundary: the approach the trace lacks: the observations between the car's exit from the stop line's stopping zone upstream and the start of the recording, in which the halt the duty requires could have been made

param_proposals.name: p.standstill_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Standstill convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed reading is read as the definition's complete cessation from movement, set at the noise floor of vehicle speed measurement so that a standing vehicle is not reported as moving and a creeping one is not reported as halted.
param_proposals.source: stop-detection thresholds used in naturalistic-driving and vehicle-dynamics data reduction

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Stop-point convention of the approach reading: the bound within which a halt counts as at the place the words name (the crossing, the stop line, the view point), covering the lateral and longitudinal error of the map's mark and of the body outline.
param_proposals.source: stop-line compliance field studies and lane-level map accuracy specifications

param_proposals.name: p.intersecting_way_view_distance
param_proposals.convention: Intersection sight-distance convention: the length of the intersecting way that must be visible in each direction from the stopping point for a driver to judge a gap and clear the junction, taken from the departure sight triangle for a minor-road stop at a major road of ordinary speed.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book, intersection sight distance (case B)

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle:
Shall not back into an intersection, on or over a crosswalk, or around a
street
corner.

elements.justification: “vehicle” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines and the run admits as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, so the span claims ru.aggregate with that id: “membership of a legal aggregate … true when the user carries an included class, unknown when no included class holds and the user carries an unresolved class”. The exclusion “not a stand-in for a named road-user class” is respected (the aggregate is claimed as the aggregate, never expanded into classes), and the exclusion of relational roles is respected by reading “driver” through controlled motion (narrowing on this span).

“back” is rearward motion: drv.motion.reverse_travel states that the component of the road user's velocity along its own heading is rearward beyond a tolerance, which is how the ontology directs the word to be read — kin.gear “is not a stand-in for the direction of motion — a vehicle in a forward gear rolls backwards on a grade; backing is read from kinematics”. “into an intersection” is the entry event into st.intersection, “the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges”, whose contract also carries the definition's third clause, since “a junction where an alley meets another way … is no intersection but a st.driveway_or_alley_entrance”, matching DEF-NRS-484A-105(3). “on or over a crosswalk” is st.crosswalk, “marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection; marked attribute”, which is DEF-NRS-484A-065's two limbs. rel.occupies, “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (… intersection, crosswalk …)”, is the anchor for both places: the entry is its rise for the junction, and being on or over the crossing is the overlap itself.

A corner is the corner of a junction of ways: st.intersection is “the region where two roadways meet”, st.highway “the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority when any part of the way is open to the use of the public for purposes of vehicular traffic” — DEF-NRS-484A-265's observable content for “street” — and st.on_way, “the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on … an intersection lies on every way that meets there”, is what makes the junction one of two ways rather than a bare region. rel.occupies anchors the corner to the subject: the vehicle's footprint overlaps that junction region. “around” is the bending of the path through the corner, carried by drv.motion.turning, whose heading change over the window behind the observation stands clear of the source's resolution; the words name no angle, so the turn is read by its presence, with parameters that name only the window and the resolution.

assumptions.meaning: the map or trace declares that the highway the road user occupies at the observation lies inside the territorial limits of a city

applicability: The bound road user is a vehicle of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle whose motion is observed. The prohibition has no further trigger: it bites at any observation at which the vehicle is travelling rearward.
obligation: At no observation may the vehicle, while travelling rearward (drv.motion.reverse_travel with p.reverse_speed_tolerance), (a) first bring its footprint to overlap an intersection region — the rise of rel.occupies on that region, which is the backing into it; (b) have its footprint overlap a crosswalk region; or (c) be turning (drv.motion.turning with p.turn_recognition_window and p.heading_change_noise_floor) while its footprint overlaps the region where two highways meet and the assumption asm.inside_city_limits holds for that highway. The three limbs are read as a disjunction, so a decided limb decides the duty even where another is unknown for want of the city-limits declaration.

narrowings.why: “The driver of a vehicle” is read as the vehicle whose motion is controlled: who or what controls a road user is not observable, and the ontology reads “the driver” through the vehicle's controlled motion, the duty binding that vehicle's conduct.

“back into an intersection” is read as the observation at which the rearward-moving vehicle's footprint first overlaps the junction, not as the whole period in which it stands within it: the words forbid the backing into the region, so the event is its entry, while “on or over a crosswalk” is read as the overlap itself, which is what those words state.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car stops just short of a four-way junction, selects reverse and then — having overshot — reverses the other way: at one observation its velocity has a rearward component of 1.5 m/s along its heading and its footprint first overlaps the junction region. It has backed into an intersection.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same car reverses 10 m along a straight stretch of roadway midway between two junctions to leave a parking bay. Through the whole reverse its footprint overlaps no intersection and no crosswalk, and it occupies no region where two highways meet, so no limb of the prohibition is met.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A pedal cycle propelled by human power, which the vehicle definition leaves out, is wheeled backwards over a marked crossing at a junction. No vehicle is bound and the rule does not engage.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The forbid scene with the source declaring road-user velocity absent: the junction, the footprint overlap and its rise are recorded, but whether the car's motion was rearward along its heading cannot be read, so the prohibition is unknown rather than satisfied.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A van reverses out of a loading bay and its footprint comes to overlap a marked crossing laid across the roadway away from any junction, its rearward speed 1 m/s. It has backed on or over a crosswalk.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A car reverses through the corner of a junction of two highways inside a city, the trace declaring the city-limits assumption true: while its footprint overlaps the junction its heading change over the window behind exceeds the resolution, so it is turning, and its motion is rearward throughout.

param_proposals.name: p.reverse_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Rearward-motion convention: the magnitude of the velocity component along the body's heading below which a rearward reading is indistinguishable from measurement noise in a standing vehicle, set at the noise floor of vehicle speed measurement.
param_proposals.source: stop-detection and direction-of-travel thresholds in vehicle-dynamics data reduction

param_proposals.name: p.turn_recognition_window
param_proposals.convention: Manoeuvre-recognition convention: the window behind an observation over which a yaw rate is integrated to tell a bending path from straight running at a junction, taken from the duration of a low-speed corner manoeuvre.
param_proposals.source: manoeuvre-segmentation windows used in naturalistic-driving analyses

param_proposals.name: p.heading_change_noise_floor
param_proposals.convention: Resolution convention: the heading change over the recognition window below which an integrated yaw reading is indistinguishable from straight running at the acquisition profile's sampling rate; it names the source's resolution only and no size of turn.
param_proposals.source: yaw-rate sensor and scene-graph heading resolution figures

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
shall not follow another vehicle
more closely than is reasonable and prudent, having due regard for the speed of such vehicles and the traffic upon and the condition of the highway.

elements.justification: “vehicle” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines and the run admits as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, so the span claims ru.aggregate with that id: “membership of a legal aggregate … true when the user carries an included class”. The aggregate is claimed whole, never expanded into classes, and “driver” is read through controlled motion (narrowing on this span), honouring the atom's exclusion of relational roles.

“follow another vehicle” is a relation between two road users over time, so it maps to a concept: drv.interaction.following states that the other road user is ahead of the subject in the same lane along the lane's direction and that the two headings are aligned within a tolerance, built on rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, “a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction”, and rel.same_direction. “another vehicle” is the same defined term, so the followed road user also claims ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, and “another” is the exclusion of the subject itself, which the formula language states with same. The followed vehicle is quantified inside the obligation and is no binder: the duty exists without it, and a subject alone must be judged compliant rather than left unjudged.

operationalizations.standard: more closely than is reasonable and prudent, having due regard for the speed of such vehicles and the traffic upon and the condition of the highway
operationalizations.convention: Time-headway and stopping-distance convention (the two-second-rule family with surface-dependent multipliers, over AASHTO perception-reaction time and stopping-distance figures). Following is closer than the bound where the longitudinal component of rel.surface_gap, “the distance between the nearest points of two bodies … its longitudinal and lateral components … along and across the subject's heading”, is less than H × kin.speed of the subject + p.following_reaction_time × the excess of the subject's speed over the followed vehicle's speed where that excess is positive + T. Each named factor is read by its degree. “the speed of such vehicles”: the subject's measured speed scales the whole headway term, so the bound grows with it, and the followed vehicle's measured speed enters through the closing speed, so a bound that is adequate behind a vehicle running at the same speed is not adequate behind a slower one. “the condition of the highway”: H is selected among bounds by the conditions read at the observation — p.following_headway_time_ice where env.ice_or_snow (“road surface icy or snow-covered”), else p.following_headway_time_wet where env.wet_road (“road surface wet, standing water”) or env.precipitation, else p.following_headway_time_adverse_geometry where the magnitude of st.grade exceeds p.following_grade_threshold or st.curvature, “horizontal curvature of the roadway at a point, as a magnitude”, exceeds p.following_curvature_threshold, else p.following_headway_time_dry. “the traffic upon the highway”: T adds p.following_dense_traffic_gap_increment where the count of road users occupying the highway the subject is on (rel.occupies with st.highway) reaches p.following_dense_traffic_count — the posted definition of traffic covering “pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel”, so every road user on the way is counted and no class narrows the stream — and is zero otherwise, so the density of the stream moves the bound. drv.interaction.following fixes which pair the bound is applied to. Every magnitude is a named parameter of the reading; the law states none.

applicability: The bound road user is a vehicle of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle whose motion is observed. The duty has no further trigger: it bites at any observation at which the vehicle is following another vehicle, which the obligation quantifies.
obligation: At no observation may there be another road user, distinct from the subject and a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, which the subject is following (drv.interaction.following with p.same_direction_cosine_tolerance) and whose longitudinal surface gap from the subject is below the bound the operationalization of s3 sets at that observation. Where no such road user is in the scene the duty is complied with; where the gap, a speed or a surface condition the selected bound reads is unobserved for a road user the subject is following, the duty is unknown. The node is a surrogate: the standard is the whole measure of the duty, so its verdicts are evidence and not a legal conclusion.

narrowings.why: “The driver of a vehicle” is read as the vehicle whose motion is controlled: who or what controls a road user is not observable, and the ontology reads “the driver” through the vehicle's controlled motion.

“the condition of the highway” is read through the contracts the ontology carries for a condition of the way — the wetness of the surface, ice or snow on it, falling precipitation, the longitudinal slope and the horizontal curvature at the point — and through no other condition. Conditions of a way the vocabulary does not carry (a broken or rutted surface, loose gravel, a worn marking) are not read, so the bound is the one those contracts support and no wider.

“the traffic upon … the highway” is read as the number of road users occupying the highway the subject is on at the observation, the posted definition of traffic covering every road user using the highway for travel. The density of the stream is the aspect of the factor the vocabulary carries; the composition of the stream, its lane discipline and its queueing are read only through that count.

“reasonable and prudent” is the whole measure of the duty, so the node is marked surrogate: the bound the operationalization states is a policy choice of the reading, not a reading of the words, and the verdicts are evidence only.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a wet single-carriageway highway a car runs at 25 m/s in the same lane as, and 20 m behind, a van travelling at the same speed, their headings aligned. The wet-surface headway bound requires about 75 m, so the longitudinal surface gap is far below the bound.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same pair on a dry, level, straight highway with light traffic: the car runs at 25 m/s with a longitudinal surface gap of 90 m behind the van, which exceeds the dry-surface bound and the closing-speed term, the two speeds being equal.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A pedal cycle propelled by human power, which the vehicle definition leaves out, rides 2 m behind a car in the same lane at 6 m/s. No vehicle is bound and the rule does not engage.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The forbid scene with the source declaring the gap between bodies absent: the following relation, the speeds and the wet surface are recorded, but the quantity the bound is compared with cannot be read, so the duty is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The car runs at 25 m/s on the same wet highway with no other road user anywhere in the scene. No road user is ahead of it in its lane, so the prohibition is complied with and the verdict is decided although the only party is the subject.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A dry, level, straight highway, but the car at 25 m/s closes on a lorry ahead in its lane that is running at 10 m/s with a longitudinal surface gap of 55 m: the dry headway term alone would be met, and the closing-speed term raises the bound above the gap.

param_proposals.name: p.same_direction_cosine_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Heading-agreement convention: the cosine of the largest angle between two headings still read as the same direction, set at thirty degrees so that a vehicle in a bend or beginning a lane change is still read as travelling with the stream.
param_proposals.source: heading-tolerance values used in lane-level trajectory conflict analyses

param_proposals.name: p.following_headway_time_dry
param_proposals.convention: Time-headway convention on a dry surface: the headway that multiplies the follower's speed to give the gap within which a leader's deceleration cannot be answered, the two-second rule.
param_proposals.source: two-second-rule driver guidance and AASHTO perception-reaction time

param_proposals.name: p.following_headway_time_wet
param_proposals.convention: Time-headway convention on a wet surface: the dry headway increased for the longer braking distance of a wet pavement.
param_proposals.source: wet-pavement friction factors in AASHTO stopping-sight-distance models

param_proposals.name: p.following_headway_time_ice
param_proposals.convention: Time-headway convention on ice or snow: the dry headway increased for the much longer braking distance of an icy or snow-covered pavement.
param_proposals.source: winter-surface friction factors in highway design practice

param_proposals.name: p.following_headway_time_adverse_geometry
param_proposals.convention: Time-headway convention on a steep or curved stretch: the dry headway increased where a downgrade lengthens braking distance or a bend shortens the view of the vehicle ahead.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO grade and horizontal-curve corrections to stopping sight distance

param_proposals.name: p.following_reaction_time
param_proposals.convention: Perception-reaction convention: the time over which a closing speed is carried before the follower's brakes act, which turns the excess of the follower's speed over the leader's into an added gap requirement.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book perception-reaction time

param_proposals.name: p.following_grade_threshold
param_proposals.convention: Grade convention: the magnitude of longitudinal slope above which the design correction to braking distance becomes material, so that the headway bound moves to the adverse-geometry selection.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO grade corrections to stopping sight distance

param_proposals.name: p.following_curvature_threshold
param_proposals.convention: Curvature convention: the horizontal curvature above which a bend materially shortens the view of the vehicle ahead on an ordinary highway, a radius of about one hundred metres.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO horizontal-curve design radii

param_proposals.name: p.following_dense_traffic_count
param_proposals.convention: Traffic-density convention: the number of road users of the traffic aggregate on the subject's highway at which the stream is read as dense enough to call for the added gap.
param_proposals.source: level-of-service density bands in highway capacity practice

param_proposals.name: p.following_dense_traffic_gap_increment
param_proposals.convention: Traffic-density convention: the gap added to the headway bound in dense traffic, covering the shorter warning a follower has when vehicles ahead of the leader may brake.
param_proposals.source: car-following model jam-spacing figures

segmentation.text: The driver of any truck or combination of vehicles 80 inches or more in overall width,
which is following a truck, or combination of vehicles 80 inches or more in overall width,
shall, whenever conditions permit,
leave a space of 500 feet
so that an overtaking vehicle may enter and occupy such space without danger,
but this shall not prevent a truck or combination of vehicles from overtaking and passing any vehicle or combination of vehicles.
This subsection does not apply to any vehicle or combination of vehicles while moving on a highway on which there are two or more lanes available for traffic moving in the same direction.

elements.justification: “truck” and “combination of vehicles” are terms DEF-NRS-484A-305 and DEF-NRS-484A-050 define and the run admits as the aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-305::truck and DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles, so the span claims ru.aggregate with each id and never the class atoms ru.truck or ru.trailer_or_combination, which the aggregate's exclusion forbids as a substitute. The width is kin.extent, “the body's size along its axes about the reference point: a trace writes the half-length, half-width and half-height; a formula reads the full length, width and height, twice each”, whose width read is the overall width the words measure; the literal 80 inches is the law's own figure and is declared in literals. “driver” is read through controlled motion (narrowing on this span).

“which is following” is a relation between two road users over time and maps to drv.interaction.following, built on rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, “a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction”, and rel.same_direction. The followed road user is of the same two defined terms, claimed as the same admitted aggregates, with kin.extent's width read for the combination; the followed road user is quantified inside the applicability and is no binder, since the duty exists for the subject whether or not a scene supplies one.

“a space of 500 feet” is the clear distance between the two bodies: rel.surface_gap is “distance between the nearest points of two bodies, each body's footprint read with its own heading and extent: zero when they touch or overlap, never negative; its longitudinal and lateral components are the lengths of the vector between those nearest points along and across the subject's heading”, so its longitudinal component is the space the words measure, and its exclusion of a centre-to-centre reading is why rel.centre_distance is not used, that atom being “not a stand-in for a clearance between bodies”. rel.ahead_behind_in_lane fixes that the space is the one ahead of the subject towards the vehicle it follows. The figure 500 feet is the law's own and is declared in literals.

“overtaking and passing” is a relation between road users over time and maps to drv.interaction.overtaking, which states the same direction within a tolerance, a speed excess and the bodies drawing level (rel.same_direction, kin.speed, rel.longitudinal_overlap, rel.ahead_behind_in_lane). The three defined terms of the span claim their admitted aggregates: the overtaking road user as truck or combination, the overtaken as vehicle or combination.

“while moving” is the negation of drv.motion.standstill, the posted definition of complete cessation from movement read as a motion state. “on a highway” is st.highway, “the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority when any part of the way is open to the use of the public for purposes of vehicular traffic” — DEF-NRS-484A-095 word for word — anchored to the subject by rel.occupies and tied to the lanes by st.on_way, “the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on — a lane, roadway, shoulder …”. “two or more lanes available for traffic moving in the same direction” is st.lane, “a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles”, with st.lane_adjacency, which carries “lane ordinal within the carriageway and the count of lanes in that direction”, the count the words require, and st.lane_direction, “direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in”, which fixes that the direction counted is the one the subject travels in; st.lane_adjacency's exclusion “not a stand-in for the marking between two lanes” does not apply, the words counting lanes and not markings. “traffic” claims its admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, which fixes whose movement the lanes are available for. The literal two is the law's own figure.

operationalizations.convention: Traffic-flow feasibility convention (free-flow versus congested operation in highway capacity practice): leaving and holding a long space ahead is possible only where the stream runs freely and nothing occupies the space. The conditions permit at an observation where the subject's kin.speed, “magnitude of velocity”, is at least p.conditions_permit_min_speed, so that a queue or stop-and-go running is not read as a failure to leave the space; and where the number of road users that occupy the subject's roadway (rel.occupies with st.roadway) between the subject and the vehicle it follows, read through the longitudinal component of rel.surface_gap and rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, is at most p.conditions_permit_max_intervening_users, so that a vehicle that has moved into the space is not read as the subject's closing of it; and where no st.obstruction, “a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user”, and no dev.temporary_traffic_control, “cones, barricades, temporary signs and flashers marking works, a closure or an obstruction”, lies in that space, since a works zone or a blocked lane makes the space impossible to hold. Both magnitudes are parameters of the reading; the words state none.

residues.why: The purpose clause explains the figure the law itself fixes: the space is 500 feet, and the words “so that an overtaking vehicle may enter and occupy such space without danger” state what that space is for, adding no further requirement to the duty, which is met by leaving the stated space and breached by not leaving it. The ontology reads a purpose through the conduct it explains, and here that conduct is the leaving of the space the next words measure. The rule is held to this: no verdict of the node turns on these words.

applicability: The bound road user is a truck of DEF-NRS-484A-305::truck, or a road user of DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles whose read width is at least the literal 80 inches, and it is following (drv.interaction.following) some other road user that is likewise a truck or a combination of that width. The subsection does not apply where the subject is moving on a highway on which the count of lanes in its direction of travel is at least the literal two (s7), nor where the subject is overtaking and passing another vehicle or combination (s6).
obligation: At each observation at which the applicability holds and the conditions of s3 permit, the longitudinal component of rel.surface_gap between the subject and the road user it is following must be at least the literal 500 feet. Where that gap is below the figure the duty is violated; where the gap, or a quantity the conditions of s3 read, is unobserved the duty is unknown.

narrowings.why: “The driver of any truck or combination of vehicles” is read as that truck or combination, the road user whose motion is controlled: who or what controls a road user is not observable, and the ontology reads “the driver” through the vehicle's controlled motion.

The space of 500 feet is read as the longitudinal component of the clearance between the two bodies, measured along the subject's heading from the nearest point of its own body to the nearest point of the body ahead, which is the quantity the vocabulary carries for a space between vehicles; a centre-to-centre distance would overstate the space by about the two half-lengths.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a two-lane rural highway with one lane in each direction, an articulated lorry runs at 22 m/s about 60 m behind another articulated lorry in the same lane, headings aligned. No road user is between them, no works or obstruction lies in the space, and the subject is well above the free-flow speed, so the conditions permit; the longitudinal gap is far below 500 feet.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same two lorries on the same highway at the same speed, but the follower holds a longitudinal gap of about 260 m, which exceeds 500 feet.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A passenger car — neither a truck of the truck aggregate nor a coupled combination, and 70 inches wide — follows an articulated lorry at 60 m on the same two-lane highway. The subject is outside the classes the subsection binds and the rule does not engage.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The forbid scene with the source declaring the gap between bodies absent: both road users' classes, the following relation and the single-lane carriageway are recorded, but the space cannot be read, so the duty is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The same two lorries at 60 m, moving on a dual carriageway whose lane adjacency records three lanes in their direction of travel. The second exception applies by its own words and the subsection does not apply.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: On the two-lane highway the following lorry is overtaking and passing the lorry ahead: the two travel in the same direction, the follower's speed exceeds the leader's by 4 m/s and their bodies' projections on the follower's heading overlap as it draws level. The first exception applies and the duty does not bite on the closed space.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: The follower lorry is held at 2 m/s in a slow-moving queue on the two-lane highway, 15 m behind the lorry ahead, with a van that has moved into the space between them. Its speed is below the free-flow bound and a road user occupies the space, so the conditions do not permit and no space of 500 feet is owed at that observation.

param_proposals.name: p.same_direction_cosine_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Heading-agreement convention: the cosine of the largest angle between two headings still read as the same direction, set at thirty degrees so that a vehicle in a bend is still read as travelling with the stream.
param_proposals.source: heading-tolerance values used in lane-level trajectory conflict analyses

param_proposals.name: p.overtaking_min_speed_excess
param_proposals.convention: Passing convention: the excess of the overtaking road user's speed over the overtaken one's below which the two are keeping station rather than passing, set at the resolution of a speed difference.
param_proposals.source: overtaking-manoeuvre identification thresholds in trajectory data studies

param_proposals.name: p.conditions_permit_min_speed
param_proposals.convention: Traffic-flow feasibility convention: the speed below which running is queued or stop-and-go, so that holding a long space ahead is not possible, taken from the boundary between congested and free-flow operation.
param_proposals.source: speed-flow curves and congested-regime boundaries in highway capacity practice

param_proposals.name: p.conditions_permit_max_intervening_users
param_proposals.convention: Traffic-flow feasibility convention: the number of other vehicles that may occupy the space ahead before the subject is read as unable to hold it, since a vehicle that moves into the space closes it without any act of the subject.
param_proposals.source: gap-closure observations in heavy-vehicle platooning field trials

param_proposals.name: p.standstill_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Standstill convention: the speed at or below which a sampled reading is read as a complete cessation from movement, set at the noise floor of vehicle speed measurement.
param_proposals.source: stop-detection thresholds used in naturalistic-driving data reduction

segmentation.text: Motor vehicles being driven upon any highway
outside of a business district
in a caravan or motorcade,
whether or not towing other vehicles,
shall be operated to allow sufficient space between each such vehicle or combination of vehicles
so as to enable any other vehicle or combination of vehicles to enter and occupy such space without danger.

elements.justification: “motor vehicle” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-130 defines and the run admits as DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle, so the span claims ru.aggregate with that id and not the class atom ru.motor_vehicle, which the aggregate's exclusion forbids as a substitute. “upon any highway” is st.highway, “the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority when any part of the way is open to the use of the public for purposes of vehicular traffic”, which is DEF-NRS-484A-095's words, anchored to the subject by rel.occupies, “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”, so the rule reads the way the subject is on and not any way of the scene. “being driven” is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (narrowing on this span): the negation of drv.motion.standstill states that it is moving, which is the observable content of the words.

“in a caravan or motorcade” is a relation between road users over time — several travelling together one behind another — so it maps to a concept: drv.interaction.vehicle_file states that, counting the subject, at least a minimum number of road users travel in the subject's direction within a tolerance, lie ahead of or behind it in the same lane, and are within a reach of it, built on rel.same_direction, rel.ahead_behind_in_lane and rel.surface_gap. Its atoms are the concept's and count as this node's through the call.

“space between each such vehicle or combination of vehicles” is the clear distance between the bodies of the members: rel.surface_gap is “distance between the nearest points of two bodies … its longitudinal and lateral components are the lengths of the vector between those nearest points along and across the subject's heading”, and its longitudinal component is the space the words mean; rel.centre_distance is excluded by its own contract as “not a stand-in for a clearance between bodies”. rel.ahead_behind_in_lane fixes that the space is the one between the subject and the member in front of or behind it in the same lane, and drv.interaction.vehicle_file fixes which road users are “each such vehicle”. “vehicle or combination of vehicles” claims the admitted aggregates for the members: the caravan's members are the motor vehicles of s1, and a member drawing another vehicle is a combination of DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles.

operationalizations.standard: so as to enable any other vehicle or combination of vehicles to enter and occupy such space without danger
operationalizations.convention: Gap-acceptance convention for a lane-change entry (the critical-gap family used in capacity and merging analysis): a space admits an entering vehicle where it holds the vehicle's own length plus a clear headway in front of and behind it at the speed of the stream. The space is sufficient at an observation where the longitudinal component of rel.surface_gap between the subject and the adjacent member of the file is at least p.entry_vehicle_length + 2 × p.entry_clearance_headway_time × kin.speed of the subject. kin.extent, “the body's size along its axes … a formula reads the full length, width and height, twice each”, is what p.entry_vehicle_length stands for: where a road user that is not a member of the file is in the scene, the length in the bound is the greater of p.entry_vehicle_length and that road user's own read length, so the degree of the factor is read where it is observed and the design length is the floor, never a reduction of the space owed. kin.speed scales the clearance term, so the space required grows with the speed of the file. “without danger” is bounded by those clearances and by nothing else; both magnitudes are parameters of the reading, and the law states no figure.

assumptions.meaning: the map or trace declares that the stretch of highway the road user occupies at the observation lies outside a business district

residues.why: “whether or not towing other vehicles” imposes no condition: it states that the duty is the same for a member drawing another vehicle and for one that is not, so no verdict of the node turns on these words. The rule is held to that: the applicability reads nothing from them, and the members of the file are read whether or not any of them draws another vehicle.

applicability: The bound road user is a motor vehicle of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle that is moving and whose footprint overlaps a highway, that is a member of a file of road users travelling one behind another (drv.interaction.vehicle_file with p.caravan_min_members, p.caravan_max_member_gap and p.same_direction_cosine_tolerance), and for which the assumption asm.outside_business_district holds for the stretch of highway it occupies. Where that assumption is not declared, whether the rule applies is unknown.
obligation: At each observation at which the applicability holds, the longitudinal component of rel.surface_gap between the subject and each member of the file immediately ahead of or behind it in the same lane must be at least the space the operationalization of s6 sets at that observation. Where a gap falls below that bound the duty is violated; where a gap, the speed or the length the bound reads is unobserved for such a member, the duty is unknown; where the subject is in no file, the rule does not apply.

narrowings.why: “shall be operated to allow … space” is read as the vehicle's own conduct: who or what controls it is not observable, so the duty binds the motion of the motor vehicle, whose spacing from the members ahead of and behind it is what the rule reads.

“each such vehicle or combination of vehicles” is read as the members of the file immediately ahead of and behind the subject in the same lane, not as every pair of members of the file: the duty binds the subject's own conduct, and the space the subject allows is the space between it and its neighbours. The spacing of a pair neither of which is the subject is that pair's own duty under the same node.

“without danger” is read through the clearances an entering vehicle needs — its length and a headway in front of and behind it at the speed of the file — and through no other aspect of danger; the manner of the entering vehicle's driving and the conditions of the surface are not read into this standard, which the words tie to the entering and occupying of the space.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Five cars of a motorcade run in file in the same lane of a two-lane highway outside a business district, declared as such by the map, at 20 m/s with longitudinal gaps of about 6 m between consecutive bodies. The space holds no entering vehicle's length plus a clear headway at that speed.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same five cars at the same speed on the same highway, each holding about 70 m of longitudinal gap to its neighbours: every space exceeds an entering vehicle's length plus the clearance headway fore and aft.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A pedal cycle propelled by human power, which the motor-vehicle definition leaves out, rides in close file with four others on the same highway. No motor vehicle is bound and the rule does not engage.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The forbid scene with the source declaring the gap between bodies absent: the file, the speeds and the declared district class are recorded, but the spaces the bound is compared with cannot be read, so the duty is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A single car runs at 20 m/s on the same highway outside a business district with no other road user anywhere in the scene. The minimum member count of the file is not reached, so the subject is in no caravan and the rule does not apply, the verdict being decided although the only party is the subject.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The five cars of the motorcade hold 6 m gaps but are halted in a queue: the subject's speed is below the standstill tolerance, so it is not being driven, and the rule does not reach a halted file. The verdict is decided on the words of the subject span.

param_proposals.name: p.standstill_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Standstill convention: the speed at or below which a sampled reading is read as a complete cessation from movement, set at the noise floor of vehicle speed measurement.
param_proposals.source: stop-detection thresholds used in naturalistic-driving data reduction

param_proposals.name: p.same_direction_cosine_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Heading-agreement convention: the cosine of the largest angle between two headings still read as the same direction, set at thirty degrees so that a vehicle in a bend is still read as travelling with the file.
param_proposals.source: heading-tolerance values used in lane-level trajectory conflict analyses

param_proposals.name: p.caravan_min_members
param_proposals.convention: Procession convention: the number of road users travelling one behind another at which the group is read as a file rather than as two vehicles happening to follow one another, taken from the smallest group that presents a continuous obstacle to an entering vehicle.
param_proposals.source: convoy and platoon definitions in traffic-operations practice

param_proposals.name: p.caravan_max_member_gap
param_proposals.convention: Procession convention: the reach within which another road user is read as travelling with the subject in the same file, beyond which the two are independent vehicles on the same highway.
param_proposals.source: platoon-identification headway and spacing thresholds in traffic-flow studies

param_proposals.name: p.entry_vehicle_length
param_proposals.convention: Gap-acceptance convention: the length of the design vehicle that must fit into the space, used where no entering road user is in the scene whose own read length could be used instead.
param_proposals.source: design-vehicle dimensions for a passenger car in highway geometric design

param_proposals.name: p.entry_clearance_headway_time
param_proposals.convention: Gap-acceptance convention: the clear headway in front of and behind an entering vehicle, at the speed of the stream, below which the entry is not a safe one; the critical gap is the vehicle's length plus twice this headway.
param_proposals.source: critical-gap values for lane-change and merging manoeuvres in capacity analysis

segmentation.text: Upon a highway designated and signposted for one-way traffic
a vehicle
shall be driven only in the direction designated.

elements.justification: “a highway” is st.highway, “the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority when any part of the way is open to the use of the public for purposes of vehicular traffic”, which is DEF-NRS-484A-095's words; rel.occupies anchors it to the subject and st.on_way, “the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on”, ties the travelled region to that way. “designated … for one-way traffic” is carried twice over, as the ontology's vocabulary carries it: st.one_way_roadway is the “roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction”, a refinement of st.roadway, and st.lane_direction is the “direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in — a lane, reserved lane, turn lane, bicycle lane or path, or a roadway, one-way roadway or shoulder”, which is the designation the next span reads; st.travel_region is the kind the quantifier over the travelled region ranges over, the abstract union that admits the lane, roadway, one-way roadway and shoulder the direction may be carried on. “signposted” is dev.regulatory_sign with code one_way, “a point regulation by catalogue code … one_way”, tied to the region by dev.governs, “the travel regions whose traffic the device controls”, and its conditions are read by prim.conditions_hold, “the structured conditions of a device … hold at the observation”, since the sign's row directs that its conditions are read that way (unconditional when empty, unknown when absent); dev.regulatory_sign's exclusion “not a stand-in for a manoeuvre or a road feature” does not apply, because the designated direction itself is read from st.lane_direction and the sign carries only the posting. “traffic” claims its admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic — “pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel” — which fixes whose travel the one-way designation governs.

“vehicle” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines and the run admits as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, so the span claims ru.aggregate with that id: “membership of a legal aggregate … true when the user carries an included class, unknown when … an included or unresolved class it might carry is unobserved”. The aggregate is claimed whole and never expanded into classes.

“driven only in the direction designated” compares the vehicle's direction of travel with the designated direction of the region it occupies: drv.position.direction_component is the component of its velocity along that region's designated direction, positive with the designation and negative against it, built on kin.velocity, “velocity vector”, and st.lane_direction, read normalised as that atom's contract directs. rel.occupies is the anchor that makes the region the vehicle's own, and st.travel_region the kind its quantifier ranges over, the abstract union that admits the lane, one-way roadway, roadway and shoulder a designated direction may be carried on. “driven” is read through controlled motion (narrowing on this span); kin.heading is not read, because a vehicle may point one way while moving another and the words govern the direction it is driven in.

applicability: The bound road user is a vehicle of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle whose footprint overlaps a travel region that lies on a highway and that carries a designated direction of travel, where a regulatory sign of code one_way governs that region and its posted conditions hold at the observation. Where the sign's governance or its conditions are unobserved, whether the rule applies is unknown; where no such sign governs the region, the rule does not apply.
obligation: At each observation at which the applicability holds, the component of the vehicle's velocity along the designated direction of the region it occupies (drv.position.direction_component) must not be at or below the negative of p.wrong_way_speed_tolerance: a component below that is travel against the designated direction and the duty is violated. A component above it — travel with the designation, a standstill, or a movement across the region within the tolerance — complies. Where the velocity or the region's designated direction is unobserved the duty is unknown. Where the vehicle occupies several such regions and the verdict differs between them, the duty is unknown; where it is the same through each, it is decided.

narrowings.why: “designated and signposted” is read as the presence of a one-way regulatory sign governing the region and of a designated direction of travel on it. That a sign or a designation is official or posted by an authority is a legal status the ontology reads through the feature itself: the sign's presence on the road is the evidence of the designation.

“shall be driven” is read as the vehicle's controlled motion: who or what controls a road user is not observable, and the ontology reads “drives” and “is driven” through the vehicle's motion, a vehicle moving on the road being taken to be driven.

“the direction designated” is read as the designated direction of travel of the travel region the vehicle occupies, and the comparison is made on the component of its velocity along that direction. A standstill and a purely lateral movement fall within the tolerance and are not read as travel against the designation, because a component of that size is not distinguishable from measurement noise; the tolerance names only that resolution.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car travels at 8 m/s along a one-way roadway of a city street whose designated direction of travel runs the other way, a one-way regulatory sign with no posted conditions governing that roadway. The component of its velocity along the designated direction is about minus 8 m/s.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same car on the same signposted one-way roadway travelling at 8 m/s with the designated direction: the component of its velocity along that direction is about plus 8 m/s.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car travels along a two-way roadway against the flow in the oncoming lane. No one-way regulatory sign governs the region it occupies, so the trigger of this subsection fails and the rule does not engage.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The forbid scene with the source declaring the designated direction of travel of structures absent: the one-way sign and its governance of the roadway are recorded and the car's velocity is recorded, but the direction the words compare it with cannot be read, so the duty is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The car stands still, loading, on the signposted one-way roadway with its body pointing against the designated direction. The component of its velocity along that direction is zero, within the tolerance, so it is not being driven against the designation and nothing in the scene but the subject decides the verdict.

param_proposals.name: p.wrong_way_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Direction-of-travel convention: the magnitude of the velocity component along a designated direction below which travel against that direction is not distinguished from standing, from lateral drift, or from the error of the mapped direction and the measured velocity.
param_proposals.source: wrong-way-driving detection thresholds in traffic-surveillance practice

segmentation.text: If a highway has two or more clearly marked lanes for traffic traveling in one direction,
vehicles must:
Not be moved from that lane
until the driver has given the appropriate turn signal
and ascertained that such movement can be made with safety.

elements.justification: “a highway” is st.highway, “the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority when any part of the way is open to the use of the public for purposes of vehicular traffic”, DEF-NRS-484A-095's words, anchored to the subject by rel.occupies and tied to the lanes by st.on_way, “the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on — a lane, roadway, shoulder …”. “two or more … lanes … traveling in one direction” is st.lane, “a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles”, with st.lane_adjacency, which carries “lane ordinal within the carriageway and the count of lanes in that direction”, the count the words require, and st.lane_direction, “direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in”, which fixes that the lanes counted are those of one direction — the direction of the lane the subject occupies. st.lane's exclusion “not a stand-in for a half of the roadway or a lateral position within a lane” is respected: the rule reads the mapped lanes and their count, not an offset from the edge. “clearly marked” is read through st.lane_marking, “per side of a lane: type ∈ {none, broken, solid, double_solid, solid_broken, dotted, curb}, colour …”: a lane marked on the side the movement crosses carries a marking of a type other than none, and the clarity of the paint is not modelled (narrowing on this span). “traffic” claims its admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, which fixes whose travel the lanes are for. The literal two is the law's own figure.
“vehicles” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines and the run admits as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, so the span claims ru.aggregate with that id and never the classes it covers.

“moved from that lane” is a manoeuvre and maps to a concept: drv.lane.lane_change states that the road user's footprint overlapped the region at the observation before and that at the observation it either no longer overlaps it or overlaps a lane adjacent to it that it did not overlap before, built on rel.occupies, “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”, and st.lane_adjacency, “left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction”. The concept takes the lane as a region formal, so the lane it reads is the one “that lane” singles out — the marked lane the trigger binds for the subject — and not any lane of the scene. st.lane is the kind that region argument admits and rel.occupies the anchor; the heading change is not read, since the words forbid the movement out of the lane and not a turn.

“the appropriate turn signal” is the signal the vehicle emits: sig.turn_indicator is “the turn indicator state ∈ {off, left, right}: neither indicator lit, or the left or the right one”, and sig.hand_signal “a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning ∈ {no_signal, left, right, stop_or_slow, re_enter}”, which is the other way the same indication is given and which the law's own scheme admits. sig.turn_indicator's exclusion “not a stand-in for the turn or lane change itself — the indicator is the signal that precedes a manoeuvre, judged separately from it” is exactly the separation these words make, the manoeuvre being s3's concept. Which indication is the appropriate one is st.lane_adjacency, the “left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction”: the appropriate signal is left where the lane the vehicle moves into is the left neighbour of the lane it leaves and right where it is the right neighbour; st.lane is the kind of both regions. “the driver has given” is read through the signal the vehicle shows (narrowing on this span).

operationalizations.standard: ascertained that such movement can be made with safety
operationalizations.convention: Gap-acceptance and conflict-avoidance convention (critical lane-change gap, with a closest-approach test over a conflict horizon). The movement can be made with safety at the observation of the change where, for every road user other than the subject that occupies the lane the subject moves into (rel.occupies with st.lane) or lies alongside the subject: the longitudinal component of rel.surface_gap, “distance between the nearest points of two bodies … its longitudinal and lateral components”, is at least p.lane_change_min_clearance + p.lane_change_entry_headway_time × the greater of the two kin.speed readings, so the required clearance grows with the speed of the faster of the pair; and the two do not close to less than p.lane_change_min_clearance within the horizon, which prim.closest_approach_within, “under constant velocities, the centres of two road users approach each other at some time between the observation and the horizon”, and prim.closest_approach_distance, “the centre distance at that closest approach”, decide over p.lane_change_conflict_horizon. drv.lane.lane_change fixes the observation and the lane the test is made for. The clearance and the horizon are parameters of the reading; the words state no figure.

applicability: The bound road user is a vehicle of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle whose footprint overlaps a marked lane L of a highway, where the count of lanes in L's direction of travel on that carriageway is at least the literal two and L carries a marking on the side the movement crosses. L is the lane the words single out as “that lane”: the obligation binds it again with the whole of that selection — a lane of the same highway, in a direction with at least two lanes, marked, and occupied by the subject at the observation before the movement — and the duty is written for every such lane the subject occupies, since the words require it of each.
obligation: At each observation at which the subject moves out of such a lane L (drv.lane.lane_change for the subject and L), the appropriate turn signal must have been given for that movement and the movement must be one that can be made with safety on the bound of s5. The signal is appropriate where sig.turn_indicator shows left, or sig.hand_signal means left, while the lane entered is the left neighbour of L, and shows or means right while it is the right neighbour; where the lane entered is no neighbour of L in L's direction, either indication given for the side the body moves towards counts. It has been given where the appropriate indication holds at the observation of the movement or at some observation in the window of p.turn_signal_advance_window behind it. Where the movement is made with no appropriate indication in that window, or where the clearances of s5 are not met at the observation of the movement, the duty is violated; where the indicator, the hand signal, a gap or a speed the bound reads is unobserved, or the window behind reaches past the start of the recording with no indication in the part observed, the duty is unknown. Where the subject does not move out of the lane, the duty is complied with.

narrowings.why: “clearly marked lanes” is read as the lanes the map represents with a marking of a type other than none on the side the movement crosses. The ontology reads the clarity of paint the same way it reads a clearly marked stop line: the marking's presence is the evidence, and its wear is not modelled. The reading relaxes nothing about which lanes are counted or which lane the duty is owed from.
“vehicles must” is read as the vehicle's controlled motion: who or what controls a road user is not observable, and the ontology reads a duty stated of a vehicle through that vehicle's conduct.

“the driver has given” is read as the signal the vehicle shows: who gives the indication is not observable, and the ontology reads such words through the observable feature — the indicator's state or the arm signal's meaning — whoever or whatever operates it.

“until the driver has given the appropriate turn signal” states no duration, so the look-back is bounded by p.turn_signal_advance_window: an indication counts as given for the movement where it holds at the observation of the movement or at some observation within that window behind it. The purpose of the bound is to give the search a stated extent, as a fixed, parameterized recognition bound rather than a search over the whole recording; a window that reaches past the start of the recording leaves the duty unknown rather than violated, so the bound never turns a signal the trace does not cover into a breach.

“ascertained that such movement can be made with safety” is read through the outcome the duty secures: the movement made with the clearances the reading sets. What a driver ascertained or perceived is not observable, and the ontology directs that a duty to perceive, ascertain or make sure is read by the outcome the check is there to secure.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a three-lane carriageway, all lanes marked and running in one direction, a car occupying the middle lane moves at one observation into the left-hand lane, its footprint reaching that lane while its indicator has shown off at every observation of the window behind and no arm signal has been given. The left-hand lane is clear.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same carriageway: the car's left indicator has been lit for two seconds before it moves into the left-hand lane, and the nearest road user in that lane is 60 m behind it at the same speed, so the longitudinal clearance exceeds the bound and the centres do not close within the horizon.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car on a single-lane one-way street, the lane adjacency recording one lane in its direction, swings onto the shoulder with no signal. The highway has fewer than two lanes in that direction, so the trigger fails and the rule does not engage.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The forbid scene with the source declaring the turn indicator absent and no arm signal observed: the lanes, the markings and the movement into the left-hand lane are recorded, but whether the appropriate signal was given cannot be read, so the duty is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The car's left indicator has been lit for three seconds, but as it moves into the left-hand lane a van is 8 m behind it in that lane and closing at 10 m/s: the longitudinal clearance is below the bound and the centres close to less than the minimum clearance within the conflict horizon.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The car, alone on the three-lane carriageway with no other road user anywhere in the scene, moves into the left-hand lane with its left indicator lit through the two observations before. The verdict is decided although the only party present is the subject.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: The car in the middle lane lights its right indicator and then moves into the left-hand lane, which st.lane_adjacency records as the left neighbour of the lane it leaves. The indication given is not the appropriate one for the movement made.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_signal_advance_window
param_proposals.convention: Signalling convention: the window behind the movement within which an indication counts as the signal given for it, taken from the advance warning a lane change is expected to carry; it is a stated recognition bound for the look-back and not a requirement of duration.
param_proposals.source: turn-signal advance-warning intervals in driver guidance and signalling-compliance studies

param_proposals.name: p.lane_change_entry_headway_time
param_proposals.convention: Gap-acceptance convention: the headway, at the speed of the faster of the two road users, that the longitudinal clearance to a road user in the lane entered must cover for the entry to be an accepted gap.
param_proposals.source: critical-gap values for lane-change manoeuvres in capacity analysis

param_proposals.name: p.lane_change_min_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Conflict-avoidance convention: the clearance between bodies below which an approach is read as a conflict rather than a safe passing distance, used both as the floor of the entry clearance and as the bound on the closest approach.
param_proposals.source: surrogate-safety-measure clearance thresholds in conflict analysis

param_proposals.name: p.lane_change_conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Conflict-avoidance convention: the time ahead of the observation over which a closest approach under constant velocities is tested, taken from the horizon used for surrogate conflict measures.
param_proposals.source: time-to-collision horizons in surrogate-safety-measure practice

segmentation.text: Every vehicle driven upon a divided highway
must be driven only upon the right-hand roadway
and must not be driven over, across or within any dividing space, barrier or section or make any left turn, semicircular turn or U-turn,
except through an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space or at a crossover or intersection established by a public authority.
